name: Flat Colour Stick Scenes
description: Round-headed stick figures with big white eyes, drawn in a thick black line whose edges stay slightly rough, standing in complete flat-coloured places, with explanatory marks drawn into the scene as objects rather than laid over it, and the joke played entirely straight.
style_bible: A drawn stick-figure world that is fully coloured and fully furnished, not an empty explainer board. Figures: where a scene asks for people, each is a stick figure with a round tan head, two big white eyes with small dark pupils and no other facial feature unless the idea needs one, a simple stick body and stick limbs with rounded ends, and hands drawn as small mittens or as nothing at all. Faces stay almost blank; whatever the figure feels is carried by the tilt of the head, the angle of the arms and where the pupils point, never by an elaborate expression. Line: everything is closed by a thick black outline of roughly even weight whose edges are visibly rough and slightly pixel-stepped, as if drawn quickly by hand at a small size and then enlarged — the contour wobbles a little, corners are not quite square, and no line is machine-smooth anywhere in the frame. Nothing is drawn twice and nothing is corrected. Fill: every surface is one flat colour with no shading of any kind — no cel step, no gradient, no ambient occlusion, no cast shadow, no highlight and no texture. Colour is the ordinary, slightly blunt palette of a hand-made diagram: grass green, sky blue, brick red, dirt brown, sun yellow, night navy, concrete grey, and the same tan the heads are drawn in. Environments: settings are complete coloured places, built from flat outlined shapes and given enough simple spatial cues to be recognisable in a second. The environment fills the frame edge to edge, and a figure is never left floating on a blank void. Diagram devices: the explaining marks are objects in the scene rather than an overlay on top of it, each drawn as a flat outlined shape that follows the surface it marks. Any lettering in this style is short, plain scene detail on an object that exists in the picture: never a headline, never a title, never a caption laid over the image and never a paragraph. Staging: exactly one clear idea per frame, staged so a viewer gets it before reading anything — one idea, one comparison or one contrast, with everything else in the environment supporting it and nothing competing for the centre. Camera is level, straight on and wide enough to hold the whole idea, with the horizon flat. Humour: gentle and deadpan. The joke is always in what is happening, never in how it is drawn; the figures never mug, never wink, never react bigger than the situation, and the picture states the absurd thing as calmly as it states the ordinary one. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed character, story, name, place, era, insignia or copied composition.
